Class EdgeHold

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.EdgeHold
public final class EdgeHold extends Object
Spacing, the half of it that is about coming in: with the opponent just out of reach and its sword ready, the fighter does not walk into that reach. It stands at the edge (W and the sprint key up) and lets the opponent come to it, into its own sword; once the opponent's sword has been spent (a swing, hit or miss) it goes in, and the crit back (JumpIn.COUNTER) is made from here.

Why. Against a player who stands at the edge of the reach, whoever steps into it first on a ready sword is hit first, and the fighter sees everything a few ticks late. On 19 October it walked into reach on a ready sword twice as often as on one coming back, and the players who space it (the spacer, the timer, the user's friend) crit it every time it did.

It does not wait for ever: an opponent that never swings first (one who only stands there) would have it standing there too. After MOST_TICKS of waiting with its own sword back it goes in anyway, and is left to do so for FREE_TICKS. Nor in its own combo (a hit of its own in the last AFTER_HIT_DEALT_TICKS ticks): an opponent that has just been hit is to be followed.

Read from what the network is shown. Not thread-safe; one per fighter.
